name: Abū ʿUmar ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar al-Thaqafī
summary: Basran grammarian and reader, student of Ibn Abī Isḥāq and teacher of al-Khalīl, said to have written the first two books of grammar, al-Jāmiʿ and al-Ikmāl.
bio: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar was a client of Thaqīf in Basra, a reader of the Qurʾān and a student of Ibn Abī Isḥāq, whose taste for analogy he shared: like him he corrected the poets. Al-Zubaydī places him in the fourth Basran generation, with Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ and al-Akhfash al-Akbar.

The sources name him as the author of two books, al-Jāmiʿ and al-Ikmāl (in al-Zubaydī al-Mukammal). In al-Zubaydī's account he was the first to build a book on what most Arabs say and to call the rest 'dialects' (lughāt), and al-Khalīl praised the two books in a couplet: 'All grammar is gone, except what ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar made: this the Completion and that the Collection, a sun and a moon for the people.' Neither book survives. He died in 149/766.
uncertain: Later authors doubt whether al-Khalīl's couplet on the two books is really his; and some think Sībawayh's al-Kitāb drew on al-Jāmiʿ, which cannot be checked.
